blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes the 1974 paper by Popek and Goldberg, which lays the foundational definitions and formal requirements for virtual machines (VMs) and virtual machine monitors (VMMs). The paper introduces a precise definition of a virtual machine as an efficient, isolated duplicate of the real machine, and a VMM as a system that provides this environment while maintaining control over system resources. The authors distinguish between privileged, control-sensitive, and behavior-sensitive instructions, and prove that a VMM can be constructed if the set of sensitive instructions is a subset of the privileged instructions. This ensures efficiency (direct execution of most instructions), isolation (resource control), and equivalence (identical behavior to the real machine). The blog highlights the paper's elegant formalism and its surprising foresight, given that the concepts were fully worked out decades before modern virtualization became widespread.
paper_title: Formal Requirements for Virtualizable Third Generation Architectures
